overview.purpose: High-performance, embeddable, multi-protocol (AMQP 1.0, MQTT 3.1.1/5, OpenWire, STOMP, HornetQ/Core) message broker in Java engineered for ultra-low latency, mission-critical throughput, append-only Direct AIO/NIO journal persistence, cursor-indexed overflow paging, non-blocking Netty remoting, distributed lock lease HA, and dual-quorum network replication.
overview.architectureType: Multi-protocol Actor-driven broker featuring non-blocking Netty I/O channels, MPSC lock-free queue ingest with PriorityLinkedList delivery, Direct AIO / libaio aligned circular append-only journal persistence, cursor-indexed multi-page file overflow paging, term-based distributed lock coordinator failover, and dual-quorum network replication.
keyDifferentiators: Non-Blocking MPSC Queue Ingestion: Decouples concurrent client producer threads from queue dispatch execution by enqueuing incoming references into a lock-free JCTools MpscUnboundedArrayQueue before single-threaded DeliverRunner polling.
Asynchronous Direct AIO Journal: Implements zero-copy aligned disk writes on Linux kernel libaio with atomic 4KB sector alignment and TimedBuffer microsecond batch synchronization.

Virtual Memory Overflow Paging: Transparently transitions addresses exceeding max-size-bytes into append-only page files, managing consumption through PageSubscription cursor indexes without exhausting heap memory.

Three-Way Dual-Quorum OperationContext: Atomically coordinates asynchronous completion across storage journal writes, network replication streams, and page syncs using atomic bitfield updaters before invoking client callbacks.

Activation-Gated Distributed HA Locks: Prevents split-brain and standby contention by restricting pluggable Curator/ZooKeeper distributed lock acquisition strictly to nodes that have completed broker activation.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Deadlock between Management removeMessage() and Paging depage() Executor
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: ThreadMXBean deadlock detection or blocked PagingStore and QueueImpl workers
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Eliminated outer synchronized(this) on QueueImpl.deleteReference() to avoid lock order inversion with depageLock.

sourceEvidence.observation: deleteReference() delegates synchronization exclusively to iterQueue() via depageLock.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: deleteReference() acquired synchronized(this) then depageLock, while depage() acquired depageLock then synchronized(this), causing deadlock under concurrent management removal and consumer depaging.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Removed redundant synchronized keyword from deleteReference(), mirroring earlier fix in copyReference (ARTEMIS-5376).

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Never nest instance monitor locks inside or outside subsystem locks (depageLock); enforce single-point synchronization within iterQueue().

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Broker Startup and Shutdown Hang on Unreachable ZooKeeper Ensemble
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Indefinite thread parking on LockCoordinator ordered executor during server shutdown
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Bounded lock manager startup with coordinator check period timeout, allowing scheduled retries.

sourceEvidence.observation: Calls lockManager.start(getPeriod(), getTimeUnit()) instead of unbounded start().

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: LockCoordinator.run() called unbounded start() which blocked indefinitely in CuratorFramework.blockUntilConnected, starving the ordered executor required for broker stop.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Bounded start call to coordinator check period; retried on subsequent scheduled execution ticks.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: All external distributed coordinator connection attempts must use finite timeouts and non-blocking retry loops.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: HTTP Tunneling Client Request/Reply Starvation Under Cluster Topology Floods
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Core client synchronous request timeouts while connected over HTTP acceptor
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Aggressive idle GET polling and HTTP response slot replenishment for server-initiated async messages.

sourceEvidence.observation: Replenishes HTTP response slots on idle GET scans to prevent server-initiated packets from draining reply channels.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Server-initiated async packets (ClusterTopologyChangeMessage) consumed queued HTTP response slots, blocking synchronous client request replies until new requests arrived.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Ensured idle polling scans replenish response slots and decoupled async notifications from client reply slots.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Separate asynchronous broadcast event channels from synchronous RPC request/response multiplexing queues in HTTP-tunneled transports.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Permanent Store-and-Forward Queue Loss After Rapid Node Cycling
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Messages accumulating indefinitely without forwarding to restarted cluster node
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Re-check cluster topology under recordsGuard immediately after record removal and re-create bridge if node is active.

sourceEvidence.observation: removeRecord() verifies if nodeID is still present in topology after record deletion.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: nodeUP topology notification arrived while stale record was present and was ignored; subsequent removeRecord removed stale record leaving no bridge and no SF queue.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Synchronized removeRecord on recordsGuard and added post-removal topology re-verification.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: State cleanup routines must re-validate current system topology before finalizing bridge disconnection.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Split-Brain Distributed Lock Contention by Passive Replicated Backup
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Passive backup holding distributed lock while acceptors and broker connections remain uninitialized
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Delayed LockCoordinator polling until broker completeActivation() runs.

sourceEvidence.observation: completeActivation() invokes lock coordinators right before starting acceptors.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: ActiveMQServerImpl.internalStart() started lock coordinators unconditionally, allowing passive backups to race and acquire locks before activation.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Split coordinator creation from startup; started lock polling strictly in completeActivation().

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Gate all HA leadership and lock leasing mechanisms behind explicit broker role activation lifecycle hooks.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Replication Channel Socket Saturation and Primary Stall
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Netty channel blockUntilWritable(0) returning false beyond maxAllowedSlownessNanos
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Disconnect lagging backup broker and release pending replication contexts to protect primary.

sourceEvidence.observation: Releases replicated packets and stops replication manager upon persistent write buffer fullness.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Slow network or blocked disk on backup filled Netty send buffers on primary, threatening to block all primary producer acknowledgements.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Implemented checkSlowReplication watchdog that isolates degraded backups.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Enforce bounded asynchronous send buffers with fail-fast disconnect watchdogs on replication streams.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Large Message File Corruption Through Divert and Mirror Routes
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Large message file deletion errors or truncated payloads on downstream mirror brokers
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Ref-counted large message file handles across divert routes and mirror controllers.

sourceEvidence.observation: Increments large message reference counters prior to diverting across mirror connections.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Large messages routed through diverts could have underlying disk files deleted prematurely if the source message was acknowledged before mirror forwarding.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Ensured proper ref-counting and file lifecycle decoupling between original message and diverted copies.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Track large message disk file handles with explicit reference counters across all routing branches.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Fix deleteReference and depage Deadlock in QueueImpl
historicalEvolution.rootCause: QueueImpl.deleteReference() held synchronized(this) while acquiring depageLock via iterQueue(), while depage() held depageLock and acquired synchronized(this).
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Removed redundant synchronized modifier from deleteReference(), mirroring the ARTEMIS-5376 fix in copyReference.

evidence.observation: Eliminated synchronized on deleteReference() to prevent lock order inversion.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Implement MQTT QoS 1 & 2 Crash Resiliency via JournalHashMap and DuplicateIDCache
historicalEvolution.rootCause: MQTT packet-ID correlations and QoS 2 PUBREC tracking relied on volatile in-memory maps that were lost on broker restart.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Persisted packet-ID assignments via generalized JournalHashMap and backed PUBREC tracking with persistent DuplicateIDCache.

evidence.observation: Stores packet ID state in JournalHashMap and drives PUBREL retransmission from DuplicateIDCache on reconnect.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Bound Lock Coordinator Start to Prevent Unreachable ZooKeeper Broker Hang
historicalEvolution.rootCause: LockCoordinator.run() started lock managers with unbounded start(-1, null), blocking the ordered executor indefinitely when ZooKeeper was unreachable.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Bounded start() call to coordinator check period; retried on subsequent scheduled execution ticks.

evidence.observation: Delegates to lockManager.start(getPeriod(), getTimeUnit()) in periodic run loop.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Activation-Gated Lock Coordinator Startup to Prevent Passive Backup Lock Theft
historicalEvolution.rootCause: ActiveMQServerImpl.internalStart() started lock coordinators immediately, allowing passive backup nodes to contend for and acquire locks before activation.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Split coordinator creation from polling; started polling strictly in completeActivation() before starting acceptors.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Fix HTTP Tunneling Server Async Packets Starving Client Request Replies
historicalEvolution.rootCause: Server-initiated ClusterTopology packets consumed HTTP response slots, causing synchronous client replies to block on responses.take().
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Ensured idle polling scans replenish response slots and prevented async broadcasts from exhausting RPC reply queues.

evidence.observation: Handles async packet dispatching with slot management that avoids client reply starvation.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Fix Race in ClusterConnectionImpl Store-and-Forward Queue Teardown
historicalEvolution.rootCause: removeRecord() was not synchronized on recordsGuard, allowing nodeUP notification to interleave between fail() and removal, causing permanent bridge loss.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Synchronized removeRecord() on recordsGuard and added post-removal topology re-check to re-create bridge if node is active.

evidence.observation: Guards removeRecord() under recordsGuard and validates topology existence.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Fix Large Message Inconsistencies Through Divert and Mirror Routes
historicalEvolution.rootCause: Large messages forwarded through diverts were susceptible to file deletion races if original messages were dropped before mirror replication.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Refactored large message handle retention in DivertImpl and PostOfficeImpl to preserve underlying disk files across routing branches.

evidence.observation: Retains message refcount and avoids premature large message file deletion.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: QueueImpl enforces strict memory threshold limits when paging mode is engaged.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: In PagingStoreImpl.writePage(), the readLock is released before timedWriter.addTask() is executed. Under high concurrent producer bursts, multiple threads pass the memory check simultaneously, causing address memory usage to temporarily exceed max-size-bytes by the size of several in-flight batch pages before flow control throttles further submissions.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: Source comments explicitly document that timedWriter.incrementTask() is called inside readLock while addTask() is called outside locks to prevent page cleanup deadlocks (found during FloodServerWithAsyncSendTest).

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Distributed lock coordinators guarantee exclusive ownership without split-brain failover windows.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: When an active primary experiences a prolonged GC pause or network partition exceeding the distributed lock lease TTL, the lock coordinator loses its ZooKeeper lease and a standby node activates. If the paused primary resumes before detecting lease loss, a transient split-brain write window occurs where both nodes accept client writes until the primary's next check-period poll.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: LockCoordinator polling operates on a periodic timer (default 5000ms); lock revocation is not synchronous with kernel I/O fencing.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: MQTT QoS 2 packet delivery counters survive arbitrary broker crashes.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: While packet ID mapping and PUBREC caches are persisted via JournalHashMap and DuplicateIDCache, transient in-memory connection session state (e.g. unacknowledged in-flight client subscriptions) can reset if failover occurs between MQTT CONNECT packet arrival and session startup CountDownLatch completion.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: Commit b30557853d73e73be1fa421f38e1b95d2c97762b documents asynchronous session startup with CountDownLatch to mitigate packet races during CONNACK.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Shared-store journal lock leasing provides instantaneous primary-to-backup failover.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: Shared-store failover relies on file lock polling (FileLockNodeManager). The backup must wait for the primary process to release the OS file lock or for lock lease expiration (default 2000-5000ms), introducing a mandatory failover latency window during which client requests block or fail.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: FileLockNodeManager periodically polls tryLock() on journal lock files with sleep intervals to avoid high NFS/SAN CPU consumption.

boundaryConditions: Network partitions isolating a primary broker from its ZooKeeper lock ensemble cause lock lease forfeiture after session timeout, forcing primary to pause acceptors while backup activates.

Sustained producer ingestion exceeding disk write throughput triggers paging mode; if page directory disk partitions fill completely, AddressFullMessagePolicy.FAIL drops messages or rejects client transactions.
Large message streams exceeding client memory limits rely on file streaming; sudden socket disconnects during transfer require background reaper threads to purge incomplete spool files.
HTTP tunneling transports subject to high-frequency cluster topology broadcasts can exhaust HTTP response slots if idle polling scans are delayed.
untestedAssumptions: Assumes underlying POSIX filesystem (ext4/xfs) provides true Direct I/O (O_DIRECT) support without fallback to kernel buffered I/O, ensuring 4KB aligned writes do not incur page cache write amplification.
Assumes network latency between replicated HA pairs is strictly lower than replication timeout thresholds (default 5000ms) to prevent false-positive backup isolation.
Assumes client SDKs implement exponential backoff reconnection logic to tolerate broker failover and topology redistribution windows.
acceptedTradeOffs: Append-only circular journal over relational table indexing: delivers massive sequential disk throughput and sub-millisecond commits at the cost of requiring periodic compaction passes to reclaim deleted records.

Lock-free MPSC enqueue over synchronized queue locking: drastically reduces producer contention on multi-core servers while delegating reference ordering and batching to single-threaded DeliverRunner iterations.

Asynchronous cursor paging over synchronous in-memory retention: allows unbounded message queues that exceed JVM heap limits at the cost of additional disk I/O and depaging latency under memory pressure.
Activation-gated lock acquisition over immediate backup polling: eliminates split-brain lock competition by passive backups while accepting a brief failover latency window during backup activation.
